title: Optimize Risk Responses
coreMove: Optimize risk responses by matching threats and opportunities to exposure, value, cost, appetite, and context, then changing the next delivery choice accordingly.

exampleSpecs.audience: new project coordinators learning the principle set
exampleSpecs.stakes: learners may memorize the title without seeing the behavior
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: learner confusion becomes the material for distinguishing vocabulary from response choices

exampleSpecs.audience: project leads defending dates under pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: schedule pressure may turn risk acceptance into avoidance of conflict
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the same status process changes once risk appetite and response fit are added

exampleSpecs.audience: PMO reviewers checking whether risk work changed choices
exampleSpecs.stakes: a tidy register may hide pressure-driven acceptance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a single detail reveals that acceptance is being used to defend the baseline

exampleSpecs.audience: project managers working through pressure alone
exampleSpecs.stakes: short-term convenience can crowd out a fitted risk response
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist works through wrong turns before selecting a fitted response

exampleSpecs.audience: project leads allocating scarce time and money before work starts
exampleSpecs.stakes: limited attention may go to the loudest risk instead of the best-fit response
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: scarce time, reserve, and sponsor attention are allocated before any action happens

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders facing a pressure test of the principle
exampleSpecs.stakes: both available responses carry visible cost
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist faces one true two-bad-options decision
